title: Grade 3 Social Studies: C3 Framework
description: Geography, local community history, civic governance, economics (goods vs services).

items.prompt: A local baker bakes fresh bread and sells it to customers in town. In economics, the baker is a:

options.text: Consumer
Producer
Banker
Governor

items.explanation: A producer is a person or business that creates, grows, or manufactures goods for others.

items.prompt: Which of the following is an example of an economic SERVICE rather than a physical good?

options.text: A haircut at the barber
A pair of running shoes
A box of breakfast cereal
A printed storybook

items.explanation: A service is work done for someone, like a haircut, not an object.

items.prompt: What is the primary purpose of the United States Constitution?

options.text: It lists every city street name
It sets prices in grocery stores
It sets the nation's basic laws and rights
It lists slang words used in America

items.explanation: The Constitution sets basic laws, rights, and how government works.

items.prompt: Which branch of local government is led by the Mayor of a city or town?

options.text: Legislative Branch
Judicial Branch
Military Branch
Executive Branch

items.explanation: Mayors lead the executive branch at the municipal city level, carrying out city ordinances and managing municipal services.

items.prompt: Which imaginary line divides the Earth into the Northern Hemisphere and Southern Hemisphere?

options.text: Prime Meridian
Equator
Tropic of Cancer
International Date Line

items.explanation: The Equator is the 0° latitude line dividing Earth into Northern and Southern hemispheres.

items.prompt: What is the economic concept of 'Scarcity'?

options.text: People have unlimited resources for every want
People get every item completely free
People have many wants but limited resources
People have too many toys to choose from

items.explanation: Scarcity means wants are many but resources are limited.

items.prompt: What type of primary historical source gives firsthand evidence from someone who lived through an event?

options.text: A diary written during the event
A modern movie about the event
A textbook written long after the event
A cartoon drawing about the event

items.explanation: A diary from the time is a primary source.

items.prompt: Why do citizens pay taxes to local, state, and federal governments?

options.text: To make officials rich and famous
To buy games and snacks for officials
To keep banks and shops open Sundays
To pay for schools and public roads

items.explanation: Taxes pay for public services such as schools, roads, and parks.

items.prompt: Which national monument in the United States stands in New York Harbor as a universal symbol of freedom and democracy?

options.text: The Golden Gate Bridge
The Statue of Liberty
Mount Rushmore
The Washington Monument

items.explanation: The Statue of Liberty in New York Harbor symbolizes freedom, democracy, and welcoming immigrants.

items.prompt: What is the difference between rural, suburban, and urban communities?

options.text: Rural has towers; urban has cows
Suburban exists only in the desert
Urban is a city; rural is open farmland
All three community types are the same

items.explanation: Urban means a dense city; rural means open countryside or farmland.
